source.title: On tuning deep learning models: a data mining perspective

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports hyperparameter and input-normalization experiments, but does not test the listed claims about training classification error, bad local minima, depth and shortcuts, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper's normalization experiment concerns min-max normalization of input features, not batch normalization. Its reported accuracy results do not measure training classification error or whether networks reach zero training error. Results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper cites batch-normalization optimization findings but tests hyperparameter search and min-max input normalization using held-out classification accuracy. Its own results do not test any listed version. Varying learning rates without measuring stability thresholds, curvature or training-loss trajectories does not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors recommend matching hyperparameters to architecture and data structure, emphasize learning rate, and conclude that normalization generally improves accuracy. Their Results identify SAE grid search as an exception; a decrease under SAE random search is not established.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies hyperparameter search and min-max input-feature normalization across DBN, FFNN, RNN, and SAE; it does not use the methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported normalization outcome differs by model and search method: RNN shows the largest stated gain, while SAE accuracy declines and grid search is adversely affected.

fits_no_version.finding: Min-max input normalization reportedly improves classification accuracy most for RNN and reduces SAE grid-search accuracy; a separate SAE random-search decrease is not established by the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-feature normalization has architecture- and search-dependent effects on held-out classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 reports classification accuracy across learning-rate choices, without stability thresholds, curvature or within-run loss trajectories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out classification accuracy depends on learning-rate choice differently across FFNN, RNN, SAE and DBN.

record.problems: The normalization findings are qualitative in the text; the cited passage provides no exact accuracy values for these comparisons. The experiment uses 24 classification data sets, but the text does not give uncertainty estimates for the reported normalization effects.
record.rows_left_out: No rows from the paper's other accuracy and hyperparameter-search results were extracted because they do not measure an outcome named by the claim versions or add a distinct finding about the claim's subject.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in large convolutional networks; corrupted labels; model-size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to the threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup alternative.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, because none of these rows measures their effects. The paper's broad normalization statements coexist with an explicit SAE grid-search exception. No version-level verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test zero or near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, or the stated model-size and training-duration conditions.
The paper does not study two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems or spurious local minima.
The paper does not compare plain and residual networks or test depth, identity shortcuts, Fixup, or deep plain tanh networks.
The paper does not compare initialization schemes or test signal and gradient propagation across depth.
The paper does not test learning rates above a stability threshold, curvature, sharpness, or divergence.
The paper tests min-max input-feature normalization, not batch normalization, and does not report training-speed or learning-rate-tolerance comparisons.
